Implementation-aligned reference

Native components, with a little glue.

A precise guide to the component lifecycle, property conversion, event wiring, binding grammar, declarative definitions, and trust boundaries of @node-projects/base-custom-webcomponent.

ESM only ES2023 target 0 runtime dependencies open Shadow DOM
01 / SCOPE

Purpose and conformance

This document describes version 0.46.0 as implemented in the repository. It distinguishes supported behavior from experimental features and known limitations.

The package is a compact inheritance-based layer over Custom Elements, Shadow DOM, templates, and constructable stylesheets. It avoids a virtual DOM and keeps advanced behavior opt-in.

A / CORE

Browser primitives first

Components remain ordinary HTMLElement subclasses. Templates are cloned into open Shadow Roots and CSS is installed through adoptedStyleSheets.

B / OPT-IN

Pay for features used

Attribute parsing, event assignment, and binding parsing are explicit protected method calls. A minimal component can skip all three.

C / TRUST

Application templates

The expression language runs JavaScript. Unprefixed text bindings can insert HTML; explicit text: and bcw:text bindings render values literally. Templates remain trusted program source, not a sandbox for untrusted expressions.

Normative security constraint A conforming application must not construct binding expressions, declarative component definitions, or bound HTML from untrusted input. Expression bindings require direct evaluation and therefore conflict with a strict CSP that omits unsafe-eval.
02 / ARCHITECTURE

Runtime model

Each component owns a cloned document fragment and an open, serializable Shadow Root. The base variant decides when that fragment is attached and when library lifecycle hooks run.

Construct host HTMLElement initialization
Attach Shadow Root Open and serializable
Clone template importNode by default
Adopt styles Sheet, array, or promise
Run chosen timing Append, setup, and ready

Design invariants

  • There is no render loop or virtual DOM.
  • State changes do not schedule updates automatically.
  • A named _bindingsRefresh(property) selects direct dependencies; an unnamed refresh reevaluates all bindings.
  • Property declarations guide attribute conversion; they are not observers.
  • Static template and style members are shared by every instance of a subclass.
  • ready() is library-defined and its timing depends on the selected base class.
03 / AUTHORING

Defining a component

Static metadata is the most portable authoring form. Legacy decorators remain available but are not required.

counter-card.ts
import {
  BaseCustomWebComponentConstructorAppend,
  css,
  html,
} from '@node-projects/base-custom-webcomponent';

export class CounterCard extends BaseCustomWebComponentConstructorAppend {
  static readonly is = 'counter-card';

  static readonly properties = {
    count: Number,
    label: String,
    disabled: Boolean,
  };

  static readonly template = html`
    <span>[[this.label]]: [[this.count]]</span>
    <button @click="increment" ?disabled="[[this.disabled]]">
      Add one
    </button>
  `;

  static readonly style = css`
    :host { display: inline-flex; gap: .75rem; }
  `;

  count = 0;
  label = 'Count';
  disabled = false;

  constructor() {
    super();
    this._restoreCachedInititalValues();
  }

  ready(): void {
    this._parseAttributesToProperties();
    this._assignEvents();
    this._bindingsParse();
  }

  increment(): void {
    this.count += 1;
    this._bindingsRefresh();
  }
}

customElements.define(CounterCard.is, CounterCard);

Template functions

html(strings, ...values): HTMLTemplateElement Creates a template by assigning its source to template.innerHTML.

htmlFromString(value): HTMLTemplateElement Equivalent string-based form.

Stylesheet functions

css(strings, ...values): CSSStyleSheet Creates a constructable stylesheet and calls replaceSync().

cssFromString(value): CSSStyleSheet Accepts text, a stylesheet, or a CSS-module-style default export.

Interpolation is not escaping Values interpolated into html or htmlFromString become template source. Use only author-controlled values. Instance data belongs in properties and bindings.
04 / LIFECYCLE

Five timing choices

The package provides deliberately explicit trade-offs between synchronous template availability, custom-element connection, and deferred initialization.

Class Append timing ready() oneTimeSetup()
BaseCustomWebComponentNoAttachedTemplate Never Never Never
BaseCustomWebComponentConstructorAppend Constructor Next microtask Once per subclass
BaseCustomWebComponentLazyAppend Next microtask After append, same microtask Once per subclass
BaseCustomWebComponentConnectedReady Constructor First connection Not invoked
BaseCustomWebComponentLazyAppendConnectedReady Next microtask First connection Not invoked
BaseCustomWebComponentConstructorAppendLazyReady Constructor Next animation frame Once per subclass

Pre-upgrade properties

The base constructor caches own properties that existed before upgrade. A derived constructor should call _restoreCachedInititalValues() after its field initializers/defaults have run.

Child definitions

_waitForChildrenReady() waits for currently undefined custom elements in the Shadow Root to be registered. It does not wait for their library ready() hooks.

05 / PROPERTIES

Attribute conversion

Property declarations form a conversion map from dash-case attributes to camel-case instance properties.

Static property metadata
static readonly properties = {
  title: String,       // title="Hello"      → "Hello"
  page: Number,        // page="3.5"         → 3.5
  enabled: Boolean,    // enabled            → true
  options: Object,     // options='{"a":1}'  → { a: 1 }
  items: Array,        // items='[1,2,3]'    → [1, 2, 3]
};
Declaration Conversion Important behavior
String Attribute text No decoding beyond normal HTML attribute parsing.
Number parseFloat() Invalid input becomes NaN.
Boolean Presence → true Absence does not actively assign false.
Object JSON.parse() Malformed JSON throws from the parsing call.
Array JSON.parse() Binding-looking strings are skipped unless noBindings is true.

Decorator status

Legacy only @property() populates the same static metadata when TypeScript emits legacy experimental decorators. Standard decorators currently throw at class evaluation time. Metadata options such as reflect are not implemented by the base class.

No automatic observation _parseAttributesToProperties() reads a snapshot. The package does not generate observedAttributes or attributeChangedCallback(). Components that need ongoing attribute observation must implement the platform callbacks.
06 / BINDINGS

Binding language

The optional parser walks element and text nodes, registers update functions, performs an initial update, and supports nested conditional and repeated templates.

Activation and refresh

Lifecycle and state update
ready(): void {
  this._bindingsParse();
}

setStatus(status: string): void {
  this.status = status;
  this._bindingsRefresh('status');
}

The parser records direct top-level dependencies such as this.status. A named refresh evaluates matching bindings and repeat descendants sourced from that property. A refresh without a property retains the refresh-all behavior. Method calls, dynamic bracket access, and unknown context expressions remain conservatively subscribed to every targeted refresh.

One-way targets

Grammar Effect Example
name="[[expr]]" Assign camel-cased DOM property value="[[this.name]]"
.name="[[expr]]" Explicit property assignment .value="[[this.name]]"
$name="[[expr]]" Set/remove string attribute $aria-label="[[this.label]]"
?name="[[expr]]" Toggle boolean attribute ?disabled="[[this.busy]]"
[[expr]] in text Write to generated container innerHTML <b>[[this.label]]</b>
[[text:expr]] in text Write literal text through textContent [[text:this.message]]
bcw:text="[[expr]]" Replace the owning element's contents with literal text <output bcw:text="[[this.status]]"></output>

The text: prefix applies only to text-node interpolation. It removes the prefix before evaluating the expression and assigns the result to textContent, so markup-like characters are displayed rather than parsed. Use [[text:?expr]] to retain the optional-value behavior that converts falsey results to an empty string.

Two-way targets

Two-way syntax
<input .value="{{this.name}}">
<input .checked="{{this.enabled::change}}">
<textarea .value="{{this.notes::change;paste}}"></textarea>

Text controls default to input; checkboxes and selects default to change; other elements default to <property>-changed. The segment after :: replaces the default event list.

Presentation directives

Directive Behavior
css:property="[[expr]]" Assigns an inline style property after dash-to-camel conversion.
class:name="[[expr]]" Adds the class for truthy values and removes it otherwise.
bcw:visible="[[expr]]" Restores the initial inline display value or applies none.
bcw:text="[[expr]]" Replaces all child content by assigning the result to textContent.

Conditional templates

Conditional rendering
<template if="[[this.hasResults]]">
  <p>Results are available.</p>
</template>

Truthy evaluation clones and parses the content. Falsey evaluation removes cached top-level element nodes. Top-level text-only template content is not reliably tracked and should be wrapped in an element.

Repeated templates

Repeat grammar
<template
  repeat:item="[[this.items]]"
  repeat-index="row"
  repeat-changed-item-callback="[[this.itemChanged(item, nodes, callbackType)]]"
>
  <button @click="[[this.select(item)]]">
    [[row + 1]]. [[item.label]]
  </button>
</template>

Local variables

item is named by the repeat: suffix. The index defaults to index and can be renamed with repeat-index. Nested repeats inherit outer locals.

Change callback

nodes contains cloned top-level elements and callbackType is "create" or "remove". A callback may replace the inserted node list by returning an iterable.

Iterables are converted to arrays. Instances are reconciled by item identity: unchanged nodes are retained, reordered nodes are moved, new identities are cloned, and removed identities are detached. Duplicate values are matched in occurrence order. There is not yet an explicit application-key expression, so equivalent replacement objects are treated as new identities. Wrap each repeated item in at least one top-level element.

07 / EVENTS

Named and evaluated handlers

Named handler assignment and expression handlers are separate mechanisms with different trade-offs.

Recommended

Named handler

<button @click="save">Save</button>

Activated by _assignEvents(). The method is bound to the component instance. It does not require expression evaluation.

Trusted templates

Expression handler

<button @click="[[this.save(item, event, sender)]]">
  Save
</button>

Activated by _bindingsParse(). It can access repeat locals, event, sender, and context values, and executes with direct evaluation.

Typed events

When a target element property with the derived event name is a TypedEvent, the parser subscribes through TypedEvent.on() rather than addEventListener().

Touch context menus

@touch:contextmenu combines the native context menu with a 500 ms touch hold. The low-level add/remove helpers are exported for manual use.

08 / DECLARATIVE

Markup-defined elements

Importing the package registers <node-projects-dce>, which can define another autonomous custom element from markup.

Declarative definition
<node-projects-dce
  name="status-pill"
  enable-bindings
  properties='{
    "label": "String",
    "active": {
      "type": "Boolean",
      "reflect": true,
      "default": false
    }
  }'
>
  <template>
    <span class:active="[[this.active]]">[[this.label]]</span>
  </template>
  <style type="adopted-css">
    :host { display: inline-block; }
    .active { color: seagreen; }
  </style>
</node-projects-dce>

<status-pill label="Online" active></status-pill>
Input Meaning
name Required custom-element name; normal platform naming rules apply.
enable-bindings Enables expression parsing and refresh for generated instances.
properties JSON object or a comma/space/semicolon-separated string-property list.
<template> Shadow DOM template for generated instances.
style[type=adopted-css] One or more constructable stylesheets.
Global and experimental surface Generated constructors are stored on window[name]. Definitions must be unique, trusted, and coordinated with the global custom-element registry. The source/module spelling “Declaritive” is retained for compatibility.
09 / API

Export reference

All current public exports are re-exported from the package root. Protected component methods are intended for subclasses.

Base component methods

Member Contract
_getDomElement<T>(id): T Returns the element with the given ID from the Shadow Root or pending fragment.
_getDomElements<T>(selector): T[] Queries the Shadow Root or pending fragment. The runtime value is the browser query result.
_assignEvents(node?): void Recursively attaches named @event handlers.
_bindingsParse(node?, removeAttributes?, host?, context?, useSignals?): void Registers and initially runs bindings. useSignals is currently unused.
_bindingsRefresh(property?, onlyWhenChanged?): void Runs bindings associated with a top-level property, or all bindings when no property is supplied.
_parseAttributesToProperties(noBindings?): void Converts declared attributes and assigns instance properties.
_waitForChildrenReady(): Promise<void> Waits for currently undefined descendant tag names to be registered.
_restoreCachedInititalValues(): void Restores pre-upgrade own-property values after derived defaults initialize.

Utility exports

Export Role Status
TypedEvent<T> Typed listener collection with on, once, single, off, emit, and pipe. Stable utility
PropertyChangedArgs<T> Container for new and old values. Stable utility
WeakArray<T> Iterable weak references with finalization cleanup. Modern browser
DomHelper Traversal, removal, indexing, host, and ancestor helpers. Stable utility
LazyLoader Dynamic classic script and text loading. Legacy-style API
debounce Leading or trailing function debounce. Stable utility
HotModuleReplacement Polling and in-place JS/CSS refresh for development. Experimental
10 / HMR

Development replacement

HMR polls a caller-supplied endpoint, reloads CSS or JavaScript modules with cache-busting query parameters, and patches known instances and class members.

Development only
HotModuleReplacement.initHMR(async () => {
  const response = await fetch('/changed-files');
  return response.ok ? response.json() : null;
});
  • The default polling interval is 100 ms.
  • Recognized extensions are CSS, JS, CJS, and MJS.
  • Instances are tracked through weak references.
  • Templates with bindings are reconstructed and reparsed.
  • Complex state, side effects, and module graphs may require a full reload.
11 / SECURITY

Trust boundaries

The safe core and the expression engine have different security characteristics. Applications should choose the smallest surface needed.

Strict-CSP capable

Core path

  • Static author-owned templates
  • Static constructable stylesheets
  • Attribute conversion
  • DOM helpers
  • Named @event handlers
  • Manual DOM updates
Trusted code only

Expression path

  • [[...]] and {{...}} expressions
  • Expression event handlers
  • Two-way paths with bracket expressions
  • Unprefixed text bindings that insert HTML
  • Markup-defined declarative components
Application requirement Prefer [[text:...]] or bcw:text for user-controlled strings. Sanitize any intentionally HTML-bearing value, keep expressions out of user control, and do not enable expression parsing when deployment policy requires a CSP without unsafe-eval.
12 / COMPATIBILITY

Platform requirements

The emitted library targets ES2023. There are no runtime npm dependencies and no bundled browser polyfills.

Feature Used by Guidance
Custom Elements, Shadow DOM, templates All components Available in modern evergreen browsers.
Constructable stylesheets css and adopted styles Broadly available across current engines since 2023.
Serializable Shadow Roots Base constructor option Baseline 2024; verify older browser targets.
WeakRef / FinalizationRegistry WeakArray, HMR, declarative instances Required only when those features are imported/used.
Direct eval() Expression bindings Requires a CSP that permits unsafe-eval.
Legacy TypeScript decorators @property Requires experimentalDecorators; static metadata is preferred.

References: Web Components, CSSStyleSheet.replaceSync(), ShadowRoot.serializable, and TypeScript legacy decorators.

13 / SAMPLES

Runnable examples

The repository includes a sample hub and three focused pages. They are compiled and exercised by the browser test suite so the examples stay aligned with the implementation.

01 / FUNDAMENTALS

Counter component

Shows lifecycle setup, number and string attributes, named DOM handlers, boolean targets, class targets, and property-specific binding refreshes.

02 / BINDINGS

Binding playground

Contrasts safe text with intentional HTML and demonstrates property bindings, conditional templates, and reconciled repeats.

03 / DECLARATIVE

Declarative definition

Defines a reusable element from HTML with typed reflected properties, an adopted stylesheet, safe text, and repeated data.

Build, verify, and serve
npm run check
npm start

Start at the sample hub to navigate between the pages.

14 / DIRECTION

Known limits and next steps

The package's strengths are its small core and direct platform model. Reliability, packaging clarity, and the binding engine are the highest-value areas for improvement.

P0 / CONFIDENCE

Broaden test coverage

The Chrome suite now covers lifecycle timing, binding targets, repeats, declarative elements, exported utilities, sample-page interactions, property upgrades, and listener disposal. Add cross-browser jobs, package assertions, malformed inputs, and deeper dynamic-import HMR coverage next.

P1 / SAFETY

CSP-safe bindings

Isolate or replace direct evaluation, make text insertion safe by default, and offer an explicit HTML directive for trusted markup.

P1 / SCALE

Explicit repeat keys

Property dependencies are now filtered and repeat instances are retained by identity. Add an explicit key expression so immutable replacement objects can preserve stateful row DOM as well.

P2 / API

Stable package surface

Add export maps and subpaths, separate development/declarative modules from the core, and align npm and JSR versions.

P2 / TYPES

TypeScript strictness

Choose standard decorators or the static property map, enable strict mode incrementally, and remove broad casts and @ts-ignore.

P2 / POLISH

Lifecycle cleanup

Track and dispose DOM and typed-event listeners, add disconnect behavior, make HMR restoration exception-safe, and fix touch context-menu removal.
